entry.title: Explicit strong blocking sets and minimal codes from expander graphs using a new graph parameter
entry.summary: A strong blocking set is a set of points in a finite projective space that intersects every hyperplane of the space in a spanning set of the hyperplane. These objects have been studied both in finite geometry and coding theory due to their equivalence with minimal codes. We give an explicit construction of strong blocking sets using expander graphs that improves the explicit construction of Alon et al. (Noga Alon, Anurag Bishnoi, Shagnik Das, Alessandro Neri, Strong blocking sets and minimal codes from expander graphs. Transactions of the American Mathematical Society ) by introducing a new geometrically motivated graph parameter that is better suited for this problem. Using this approach, we improve the constant $C$ in the explicit construction of a strong blocking set of size $C (q+1) k$ in the $(k - 1)$-dimensional projective space over $\mathbb{F}_q$ for every prime power $q \geq 7$.

entry.title: Exploring Minimal Blocking Sets for Kernelization Lower Bounds for $\mathcal{F}$-Minor Deletion
entry.summary: For Vertex Cover, a minimal blocking set of a graph $G$ is an inclusion-wise minimal vertex set contained in no minimum vertex cover of $G$. Bougeret et al. [SIDMA 2022] showed that, for all minor-closed graph classes $\mathcal{G}$, Vertex Cover has a polynomial kernel parameterized by the distance to $\mathcal{G}$ if and only if $\mathcal{G}$ has bounded minimal blocking sets. In this work, we explore how far this connection between minimal blocking sets and kernelization extends to $\mathcal{F}$-Minor Deletion parameterized by the deletion distance to $\mathcal{G}$. A minimal $\mathcal{F}$-blocking set of $G$ is a minimal vertex set not contained in any optimal $\mathcal{F}$-Minor Deletion solution of $G$. For connected families $\mathcal{F}$, we show that if some graph class $\mathcal{G}$ closed under disjoint union has unbounded minimal $\mathcal{F}$-blocking sets, then $\mathcal{F}$-Minor Deletion parameterized by the deletion distance to $\mathcal{G}$ has no polynomial kernel. This generalizes a result of Hols et al. [SIDMA 2022] for Vertex Cover. We then show that this criterion does not capture all kernelization lower bounds for $\mathcal{F}$-Minor Deletion, even for minor-closed graph classes. Motivated by the work of Dekker and Jansen [Discrete Appl. Math. 2024], we study the more general notion of extended $\mathcal{F}$-blocking sets and the kernelization lower bounds they yield. For every fixed integer $η\geq 1$, Pw-$η$ Deletion is the problem of deleting at most $k$ vertices to reduce the pathwidth to at most $η$. We show that it has no polynomial kernel parameterized by the distance to graphs with pathwidth at most $η+1$. Moreover, for connected families $\mathcal{F}$, we show that $\mathcal{F}$-Minor Deletion parameterized by the distance to graphs with pathwidth at most $\max_{F\in\mathcal{F}} pw(F)+1$ has no polynomial kernel.

entry.title: Further results on binary linear covering codes and saturating sets in projective spaces
entry.summary: The binary length function $\ell_2(r,R)$ is the smallest length of a binary linear code with codimension (redundancy) $r$ and covering radius $R$. Let $s_2(N,ρ)$ be the smallest size of a $ρ$-saturating set in the binary projective space $\mathrm{PG}(N,2)$. It is known that the binary length function satisfies $\ell_2(r,R)=s_2(r-1,R-1)$. We obtain the following new upper bounds on $\ell_2(r,R)$, improving the previously known upper bounds by $Δ(r,R)$: $R=2,r=2t\ge28$, and $r=10,18,20$, $\ell_2(r,2)=s_2(r-1,1)\le51\cdot2^{r/2-5}-1,Δ(r,2)=2^{r/2-5}$; $R=3,r=3t-1\ge41$ and $r=26$, $\ell_2(r,3)=s_2(r-1,2)\le818\cdot2^{(r-26)/3}-1$, $Δ(41,3)=63,Δ(r,3)=2^{(r-26)/3}$ if $r\ge44$. To obtain these bounds, we construct new infinite code families, using distinct versions of the $q^m$-concatenating constructions of covering codes, including new versions proposed in this paper. We also obtain new useful partitions of column sets of parity check matrices of some codes. The new code families provide the asymptotic covering-density bounds $\overlineμ(2)\le2601/2048<1.27002$, $\overlineμ(3)\le1.35935$, improving the previously known bounds and giving rise to the new upper bounds $f(2)\le2601/2048<1.27002$, $f(3)\le1.35935$ on the constants $f(2),f(3)$ of the Green's Open Problem 40.

entry.title: Detection and Construction of Small Blocking Sets via Critical Independent Sets and Matching Decomposition
entry.summary: The small blocking set detection and construction problem asks whether a given connected simple graph contains a nonempty independent set whose cardinality equals the size of its neighborhood and is strictly less than half the number of vertices, and, if so, how to construct such a set. Previous work characterized restless explorability in vertex-permuted temporal graphs using small blocking sets, but left the computational complexity of detecting their existence as an open problem. We give a polynomial-time algorithm for detection and construction. Specifically, we first compute a maximum-cardinality critical independent set and use its difference and cardinality to handle the cases that admit an immediate solution. In the remaining boundary case, where the critical difference is zero and the selected independent set contains exactly half the vertices, we establish a projection theorem using a perfect matching and neighborhood counting: the graph contains a small blocking set if and only if the selected independent set contains a nonempty proper tight subset. We then use matching contraction to translate the tight-subset condition into the absence of arcs leaving a vertex subset in an auxiliary digraph. This yields a strong-connectivity test for the existence of a small blocking set and, when one exists, a construction based on a sink strongly connected component. The result resolves the open complexity question for small blocking set detection and provides an explicit construction algorithm.

entry.title: A Simple Explicit Construction of Smaller Strong Blocking Sets
entry.summary: Alon, Bishnoi, Das and Neri constructed sequences of strong blocking sets in $(k-1)$-dimension projective space $P({\bf F}_q, k-1)$ with sizes at most $Cqk$, where $k$ goes to the infinity and $C$ is a fixed positive constant not depending on $q$, in their paper published in Transactions AMS, vol. 277, pp. 5389-5410, 2024. This is equivalent to a sequence of minimal $[n_i,k_i]_q$ codes with positive rate $\frac{k_i}{n_i} \geq c$, where $k_i$ goes to the infinity and $c$ is a fixed positive constant only depending on $q$. They solved one of the main open problems on minimal codes. The Alon-Bishnoi-Das-Neri construction was based on asymptotically good sequences of algebraic geometric codes and expander graphs. However, the constant $C$ is large for small prime power $q$. In this paper, based on a simple approach using $(q-1)$-power intersecting algebraic geometric codes via concatenation to construct minimal codes, we construct explicit strong blocking sets in $(k-1)$-dimension projective space with sizes around $2(q^2-1)k$, equivalently, explicit minimal $[n,k]_q$ codes with length around $2(q^2-1)k$. This is an essential improvement on the previous result of Alon-Bishnoi-Das-Neri, when $q \leq 11$. For large $q$, strong blocking sets and minimal codes in our construction are worse than the previous construction of Alon-Bishnoi-Das-Neri. However, our approach is much simpler and does not depend on expander graphs.

entry.title: Small 3-fold blocking sets in $\mathrm{PG}(2,p^n)$
entry.summary: A $t$-fold blocking set of the finite Desarguesian plane $\mathrm{PG}(2,p^n)$, $p$ prime, is a set of points meeting each line of the plane in at least $t$ points. The minimum size of such sets is of interest for numerous reasons; however, even the minimum size of nontrivial blocking sets (i.e. $1$-fold blocking sets not containing a line) in \(\mathrm{PG}(2,p^n)\) is an open question when $n\geq 5$ is odd. For $n>1$ the conjectured lower bound for this size is $(p^n+p^{n(s-1)/s}+1)$, where $p^{n/s}$ is the size of the largest proper subfield of $\mathbb{F}_{p^n}$. Since the union of $t$ pairwise disjoint nontrivial blocking sets is a $t$-fold blocking set, it is conjectured that when $p^{n/s}$ is large enough w.r.t. $t$, then the minimum size of a $t$-fold blocking set in $\mathrm{PG}(2,p^n)$ is $t(p^n+p^{n(s-1)/s}+1)$. If $n$ is even, then the decomposition of the plane into disjoint Baer subplanes gives a $t$-fold blocking set of this size. However, for odd $n$, the existence of such sets is an unsolved problem in most cases. In this paper, we construct $3$-fold blocking sets of conjectured size. These blocking sets are obtained as the disjoint union of three linear blocking sets of Rédei type, and they lie on the same orbit of the projectivity $(x:y:z)\mapsto (z:x:y)$.

entry.title: Cameron-Liebler sets of generators in the Klein quadric $Q^+(5,q)$
entry.summary: We investigate Cameron-Liebler sets of planes in the Klein quadric $Q^+(5,q)$ in PG$(5,q)$. We prove that there are many examples of such Cameron-Liebler sets of planes in the Klein quadric. More specifically, we provide an incomplete list of examples of such Cameron-Liebler sets of planes. By doing so, we also provide some characteristic results regarding these sets in connection with the Klein quadric. These results contribute to an open conjecture posed in [21].

entry.title: Letters, Colors, and Words: Constructing the Ideal Building Blocks Set
entry.summary: Define a building blocks set to be a collection of n cubes (each with six sides) where each side is assigned one letter and one color from a palette of m colors. We propose a novel problem of assigning letters and colors to each face so as to maximize the number of words one can spell from a chosen dataset that are either mono words, all letters have the same color, or rainbow words, all letters have unique colors. We explore this problem considering a chosen set of English words, up to six letters long, from a typical vocabulary of a US American 14 year old and explore the problem when n=6 and m=6, with the added restriction that each color appears exactly once on the cube. The problem is intractable, as the size of the solution space makes a brute force approach computationally infeasible. Therefore we aim to solve this problem using random search, simulated annealing, two distinct tree search approaches (greedy and best-first), and a genetic algorithm. To address this, we explore a range of optimization techniques: random search, simulated annealing, two distinct tree search methods (greedy and best-first), and a genetic algorithm. Additionally, we attempted to implement a reinforcement learning approach; however, the model failed to converge to viable solutions within the problem's constraints. Among these methods, the genetic algorithm delivered the best performance, achieving a total of 2846 mono and rainbow words.

entry.title: Block Sizes in the Block Sets Conjecture
entry.summary: A set $X$ is called Euclidean Ramsey if, for any $k$ and sufficiently large $n$, every $k$-colouring of $\mathbb{R}^n$ contains a monochromatic congruent copy of $X$. This notion was introduced by Erdős, Graham, Montgomery, Rothschild, Spencer and Straus. They asked if a set is Ramsey if and only if it is spherical, meaning that it lies on the surface of a sphere. It is not too difficult to show that if a set is not spherical then it is not Euclidean Ramsey either, but the converse is very much open despite extensive research over the years. On the other hand, the block sets conjecture is a purely combinatorial, Hales-Jewett type of statement, concerning `blocks in large products', introduced by Leader, Russell and Walters. If true, the block sets conjecture would imply that every transitive set (a set whose symmetry group acts transitively) is Euclidean Ramsey. As for the question above, the block sets conjecture remains very elusive, being known only in a few cases. In this paper we show that the sizes of the blocks in the block sets conjecture cannot be bounded, even for templates over the alphabet of size $3$. We also show that for the first non-trivial template, namely $123$, the blocks may be taken to be of size $2$ (for any number of colours). This is best possible; all previous bounds were `tower-type' large.

entry.title: Strong blocking sets and minimal codes from expander graphs
entry.summary: A strong blocking set in a finite projective space is a set of points that intersects each hyperplane in a spanning set. We provide a new graph theoretic construction of such sets: combining constant-degree expanders with asymptotically good codes, we explicitly construct strong blocking sets in the $(k-1)$-dimensional projective space over $\mathbb{F}_q$ that have size $O( q k )$. Since strong blocking sets have recently been shown to be equivalent to minimal linear codes, our construction gives the first explicit construction of $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear minimal codes of length $n$ and dimension $k$, for every prime power $q$, for which $n = O (q k)$. This solves one of the main open problems on minimal codes.

entry.title: Full Characterization of Minimal Linear Codes as Cutting Blocking Sets
entry.summary: In this paper, we first study in detail the relationship between minimal linear codes and cutting blocking sets, which were recently introduced by Bonini and Borello, and then completely characterize minimal linear codes as cutting blocking sets. As a direct result, minimal projective codes of dimension $3$ and $t$-fold blocking sets with $t\ge 2$ in projective planes are identical objects. Some bounds on the parameters of minimal codes are derived from this characterization. This confirms a recent conjecture by Alfarano, Borello and Neri in [a geometric characterization of minimal codes and their asymptotic performance, arXiv:1911.11738, 2019] about a lower bound of the minimum distance of a minimal code. Using this new link between minimal codes and blocking sets, we also present new general primary and secondary constructions of minimal linear codes. As a result, infinite families of minimal linear codes not satisfying the Aschikhmin-Barg's condition are obtained. In addition to this, the weight distributions of two subfamilies of the proposed minimal linear codes are established. Open problems are also presented.

entry.title: Elimination Distances, Blocking Sets, and Kernels for Vertex Cover
entry.summary: The Vertex Cover problem plays an essential role in the study of polynomial kernelization in parameterized complexity, i.e., the study of provable and efficient preprocessing for NP-hard problems. Motivated by the great variety of positive and negative results for kernelization for Vertex Cover subject to different parameters and graph classes, we seek to unify and generalize them using so-called blocking sets, which have played implicit and explicit roles in many results. We show that in the most-studied setting, parameterized by the size of a deletion set to a specified graph class $\mathcal{C}$, bounded minimal blocking set size is necessary but not sufficient to get a polynomial kernelization. Under mild technical assumptions, bounded minimal blocking set size is showed to allow an essentially tight efficient reduction in the number of connected components. We then determine the exact maximum size of minimal blocking sets for graphs of bounded elimination distance to any hereditary class $\mathcal{C}$, including the case of graphs of bounded treedepth. We get similar but not tight bounds for certain non-hereditary classes $\mathcal{C}$, including the class $\mathcal{C}_{LP}$ of graphs where integral and fractional vertex cover size coincide. These bounds allow us to derive polynomial kernels for Vertex Cover parameterized by the size of a deletion set to graphs of bounded elimination distance to, e.g., forest, bipartite, or $\mathcal{C}_{LP}$ graphs.
